structure.heading: Migration Execution Status and Cost Optimisation vs On‑Prem Baseline
text_content: **Migration Execution Status and Cost Optimisation vs On‑Prem Baseline**

As of 30-04-2026, 68 of 120 workloads (56.7%) have been migrated to cloud, meeting the programme mid‑point target. This progress reflects completed migrations across infrastructure, middleware, and selected applications, with remaining workloads prioritized by dependency, criticality, and technical fit. Migration velocity has been steady month-over-month and will be re-evaluated against programme milestones to ensure completion within contracted timelines, with executive review.

The on‑prem baseline is $1.20M per month (FY2025 run rate), and April 2026 cloud run cost is $0.92M per month (23.3% lower). Savings are primarily driven by rightsizing compute, Reserved Instance commitments, storage tiering, and reduced data centre overhead. Remaining optimisation focus areas include licence rationalisation, workload replatforming, and automated instance lifecycle management to sustain and improve run‑rate reductions. And reporting remains monthly.

18, migrating 14 workloads including CRM-App01 and DataHub-ETL. Post-cutover validation cycles were executed, rollback windows closed, and operational handover completed for transitioned services. Outstanding actions have been captured in the remediation backlog with priority SLAs; these items will inform post-cutover process improvements, runbook refinements, monitoring thresholds, and on-call staffing adjustments. And final audit scheduled.

sections.heading: Executive Summary
sections.body: As of 30 April 2026, the programme has migrated 312 of 428 in-scope workloads (73%), marking a 9% increase since the previous quarter. Cutover velocity improved following the standardisation of migration runbooks and automated landing zone provisioning. The programme remains on track to meet the FY2026 target of 85% workload migration by year-end. Cost optimisation performance continues to trend positively against the approved on-premises baseline.

sections.heading: Migration Progress and Cutover Performance
sections.body: During Q3, 54 production workloads were successfully cut over to Azure and AWS environments, including the Finance Reporting Suite and the Regional Claims Portal. Average migration cycle time reduced from 11.2 weeks to 8.6 weeks due to improved dependency mapping and pre-cutover validation testing. Two legacy Oracle-based systems were replatformed to managed database services, eliminating $420K in projected hardware refresh spend. Remaining complex workloads are concentrated in the Data Analytics and Manufacturing Execution domains.

sections.heading: Cost Optimisation vs On-Prem Baseline
sections.body: Actual cloud run-rate for migrated workloads is 18.7% below the FY2024 on-prem baseline when adjusted for inflation and licensing uplifts. Savings have been realised through reserved instance commitments, rightsizing of compute, and decommissioning of three secondary data centre racks in Milton Keynes. Storage lifecycle policies reduced monthly object storage costs by 23% compared to initial post-migration estimates. Forecast models indicate a cumulative net benefit of £6.4M by the end of FY2026 if current optimisation controls are maintained.

sections.heading: Operational Readiness and Service Stability
sections.body: Operational readiness reviews were completed for all Q3 migrations, with 96% of workloads meeting Day-1 monitoring, backup, and DR compliance standards at go-live. structure.full_text:
Cloud Migration Programme Status Report – Workload Acceleration & Cost Realisation
Ref: CMP-22-3846447 | Date: 04 May 2026 | Reporting Period: Q3 FY2026 | From: Enterprise Cloud Transformation Office

Section Executive Summary
As of 30 April 2026, the programme has migrated 312 of 428 in-scope workloads (73%), marking a 9% increase since the previous quarter. Cutover velocity improved following the standardisation of migration runbooks and automated landing zone provisioning. The programme remains on track to meet the FY2026 target of 85% workload migration by year-end. Cost optimisation performance continues to trend positively against the approved on-premises baseline.

Section Migration Progress and Cutover Performance
During Q3, 54 production workloads were successfully cut over to Azure and AWS environments, including the Finance Reporting Suite and the Regional Claims Portal. Average migration cycle time reduced from 11.2 weeks to 8.6 weeks due to improved dependency mapping and pre-cutover validation testing. Two legacy Oracle-based systems were replatformed to managed database services, eliminating $420K in projected hardware refresh spend. Remaining complex workloads are concentrated in the Data Analytics and Manufacturing Execution domains.

Section Cost Optimisation vs On-Prem Baseline
Actual cloud run-rate for migrated workloads is 18.7% below the FY2024 on-prem baseline when adjusted for inflation and licensing uplifts. Savings have been realised through reserved instance commitments, rightsizing of compute, and decommissioning of three secondary data centre racks in Milton Keynes. Storage lifecycle policies reduced monthly object storage costs by 23% compared to initial post-migration estimates. Forecast models indicate a cumulative net benefit of £6.4M by the end of FY2026 if current optimisation controls are maintained.

Section Operational Readiness and Service Stability
Operational readiness reviews were completed for all Q3 migrations, with 96% of workloads meeting Day-1 monitoring, backup, and DR compliance standards at go-live. Mean time to recovery (MTTR) for cloud-hosted services has improved to 42 minutes, compared to 68 minutes in the legacy estate. A minor incident in February related to misconfigured network security groups was resolved within SLA and led to enhanced automated policy checks. Cloud Operations has completed cross-training of 28 infrastructure engineers on FinOps and SRE practices to support steady-state operations.

Section Next-Phase Plan (Q4 FY2026)
The next phase will prioritise migration of the remaining high-complexity analytics clusters and the SAP BW environment, representing approximately 14% of total infrastructure cost. A structured application rationalisation review will target retirement or consolidation of at least 12 low-utilisation services before migration. Contract negotiations for extended reserved capacity are underway to lock in pricing before the July rate adjustment window. The programme board has endorsed the revised roadmap, confirming alignment with the FY2026 objective of 85% migration and a minimum 20% cost reduction against the original on-prem baseline.

Confidential — Internal Distribution Only | Cloud Migration Programme | Page 1 of 1
